result.title: Controlled Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models: Random Initialisation, Band-Power and Validation-Selected Probes
result.summary: EEG foundation models report downstream gains, yet their protocols seldom include three controls. These are the same encoder untrained, spectral features fitted on the same data, and a layer picked without looking at test scores. We therefore evaluate five publicly released EEG foundation models and an in-house JEPA-style model under one protocol with all three controls and several seeds, on five benchmarks and four added task families. The controls change the reading in three ways. First, picking the probed layer by its test score raises the layer-wise peak by an average of +0.034 and reverses the peak-versus-output gap in 9 of 36 cells. Second, with the layer picked on validation, random initialisation matches or beats pretraining for half of the models on sleep and emotion, and no model beats a five-band log-power baseline on emotion or motor imagery. Third, after full fine-tuning only 5 of 30 pairs gain beyond twice their seed spread, and the one clear loss of -0.290 AUROC persists under matched learning rates. From these results we draw four reporting practices, and we release every cell for re-analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 在统一协议下评测五个公开 EEG 基础模型与一个自研 JEPA 式模型，同时加入三项对照：同一编码器不训练、同数据上拟合的五频带 log-power 特征基线、以及仅依据验证集选层，并覆盖五个基准与四个新增任务族。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「未训练编码器 + 简单特征基线 + 验证集选层」的对照设计，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正贡献、而非被视觉旁路或基线解释，探针选层偏差的处理也可能迁移到 latent 表征的评测。
